newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs say Iran wants oil pipeline linking them.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs say Iran wants oil pipeline linking them.

text.p: Iranian Parliament Speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri on Thursday proposed a new oil pipeline to export Kazakh crude to western markets via Iran, Kazakhstan's parliamentary press service said on Thursday.
"Nateq-Nouri said Iran wants to reach an early agreement between our states...on building an oil pipeline and railway through Iranian territory," said a spokeswoman at the Kazakh parliament.
"They are particularly interested in our Caspian oil," she said.
Nateq-Nouri, travelling with various Iranian industry ministers, is in Almaty at the start of an Asian tour which will also take him to Turkmenistan and India.
Oil-rich Kazakhstan and Iran have been negotiating a two-million-tonne oil swap, but the deal has yet to be finalised.

The United States, which has several oil majors investing in Kazakhstan, including Chevron Corp and Mobil Corp, has pressured the former Soviet republic to do no deals with Iran because of what Washington says is Tehran's involvement in terrorism.
Under the Iran-Libya Sanctions Act signed by President Bill Clinton in August, U.S. companies will be punished if they invest over $40 million in the two countries' oil and gas sectors.
The Iranian pipeline proposal comes just before a group seeking to get its troubled $1.5 billion Caspian oil pipeline project off the ground meets in December to try to push the deal forward.
